item.title: Reflexivity of Grothendieck Spaces and Strongly Normal Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.12787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A normalized sequence $(y_n)$ in the dual $E^{*}$ of a Banach space $E$ is called normal if it is weak-star null, and strongly normal if [ G(y_n)=\left{x\in E:\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|y_n(x)|<\infty\right} ] is dense in $E$. We prove that, within the class of Grothendieck Banach spaces, reflexivity is characterized by the subsequence behavior of normal sequences: a Grothendieck space $E$ is reflexive if and only if every normal sequence in $E^{*}$ contains a strongly normal subsequence. If $E$ is nonreflexive and Grothendieck, then $E^{*}$ contains a normalized weakly null sequence none of whose subsequences is strongly normal; more strongly, it contains a closed hereditarily $\ell_{1}$ subspace $Y$ with a normalized weakly null Schauder basis such that no sequence in $S(Y)$ is strongly normal. We also obtain an exact quotient criterion valid for arbitrary Banach spaces: a normal sequence has a strongly normal subsequence precisely when, for some subsequence $z=(z_n)$, the quotient $E/\bigcap_n\ker z_n$ is separable. The proofs combine a weak-star basic-sequence argument with results of Haydon, Johnson--Maurey--Schechtman and Popov. Concrete realizations are given in $(L_{\infty}(\mu))^{*}$ for nonatomic probability spaces (and, more generally, for $\sigma$-finite spaces with a nonatomic part) and in $\ell_{\infty}^{*}$.
item.dc:creator: Wies{\l}aw \'Sliwa

item.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carath\'eodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Carath\'eodory-type extension theorem for premeasures with values in general separated abelian net convergence groups. Starting from hereditary exhaustivity on the source ring and intrinsic conditions for combining null errors, we construct a countably additive extension on a regulated Boolean sigma-algebra, with full upper and lower regularity in the original convergence. Completeness is required only on the limit-stable hull of the source range. Under closed summation for arbitrary directed rows and finite-response reflection, we identify the regulated domain with the splitting class of Sion's inner and outer processes. For a Dedekind-complete real vector lattice, we show that sequential closed summation on a bounded interval is equivalent to weak sigma-distributivity of the generated band, giving a converge-theoretic interpretation of the concept. Source representations allow us to recover the partially ordered-group extension of Volauf and the finite-variation extension of Kusraev and Malyugin from the general theorem. We then treat finite semivariation by adjoining dominated coordinate variations to an additive lift of the premeasure. The resulting extension is defined on the full semivariation regulator domain and preserves semivariation exactly, without requiring decomposability or the countable sup property. It includes measures of infinite vector variation.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira

item.title: Geometric operators and the third problem of Halmos
item.description: arXiv:2610.12857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.
item.dc:creator: Kui Ji, Chunlan Jiang, Zhenyue Wang

item.title: On Surjective Max-Phase Isometries of Schatten p-Classes (0<p<1)
item.description: arXiv:2610.13271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate max-phase isometries on Schatten quasi-classes in the range $0<p<1$. Motivated by the rigidity theory for smooth normed spaces [\emph{Results Math.} \textbf{80} (2025), Article 126], we establish its operator-theoretic counterpart in the quasi-Banach setting. We prove that every surjective max-phase isometry on a finite-dimensional Schatten class is a standard real-linear Schatten isometry multiplied by an even sign-valued function, without any continuity assumption. This extends the scope of the classical Schatten isometry classification [\emph{Proc. Edinburgh Math. Soc.} \textbf{37} (1994), 239--242] to nonlinear mappings preserving only unsigned two-point metric data. Our approach combines support orthogonality, a symmetrized rank-one spectral formula, and a max-profile uniqueness principle. For arbitrary Hilbert spaces, we obtain the corresponding classification on finite-rank operators, while continuity yields the full-space result. We also establish preservation of rank, singular values, and two-sided support orthogonality.
item.dc:creator: Wenwen Zhang, Qi Liu

item.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert--Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Li

item.title: Banach space, Birkhoff--James orthogonality, James constant, von Neumann--Jordan constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.13360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a strengthened answer to the questions posed by Alonso, Mart\'in, and Papini [Studia Math. 188 (2008), 135--150] concerning the comparison between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants . The classical inequality $\CNJ(X)\leq J(X)$ between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants was established by Takahashi and Kato [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 359 (2009), 602--609], Wang [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 138 (2010), 695--701], and Yang and Li [Appl. Math. Lett. 23 (2010), 277--281], while related sharp estimates were obtained by Kato and Takahashi [Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) Suppl. 82 (2010), 75--91]. We sharpen this inequality to $\CNJ(X)\leq\JB(X)$, where $\JB(X)$ is the Birkhoff--James orthogonal James constant introduced by Baronti and Papini [Constr. Math. Anal. 5 (2022), 37--45]. Our proof employs optimal distance ellipses and alternating contact directions.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu

item.title: On the simultaneous zero inclusion property and characterization of Inner product space
item.description: arXiv:2610.13378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if a Banach space $X$ is smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund and if satisfies the following \[0\in W(T) \implies 0\in W(T^{-1})\] for all invertible bounded linear map on $X$ then Birkhoff-James orthogonality in $X$ is symmetric. This result, therefore, characterizes the inner product spaces out of all smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces having three or more dimension via simultaneous zero inclusion property, introduced by Bra\v{c}i\v{c} et al. [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 449 (2017) 1413-1423]. Further, this gives answers to some open questions asked by E. Poon [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 534(2024), 128052].
item.dc:creator: Souvik Ghosh

item.title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations with an application to elliptic boundary value problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations on a Hilbert space. The proof relies on the Arens decomposition of a closed linear relation into an operator part and a purely multivalued part, reducing the problem directly to the classical spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators. No finite-dimensionality condition is imposed on the multivalued part. We also prove a finiterank approximation theorem for compact bounded linear relations and a Fredholm alternative for compact self-adjoint linear relations. As an application, we employ the theory of boundary triples to show that the inverse of the Neumann Laplacian on a bounded domain is a compact self-adjoint linear relation. The abstract spectral theorem then recovers the classical eigenfunction expansion of solutions to the Neumann problem: an L2-convergent series in terms of the non-constant Neumann eigenfunctions together with an arbitrary additive constant. The framework extends naturally to general elliptic boundary value problems with finite-dimensional kernel.
item.dc:creator: Mathew Thomas, V. B. Kiran Kumar

item.title: A Vector-Valued Extension of a Theorem of Marciszewski
item.description: arXiv:2610.13414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a vector-valued extension of a theorem of Marciszewski. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $\Gamma$ be a set, and let $X$ be a nonzero Banach space containing no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. We prove that if $C(K)$ embeds isomorphically into $c_0(\Gamma,X)$, then $C(K)$ is isomorphic to $c_0(\Lambda)$ for some set $\Lambda$. Moreover, when $\Gamma$ is infinite, the optimal distortion of embeddings of $C(K)$ into $c_0(\Gamma,X)$ equals that of embeddings into $c_0(\Gamma)$. The classification result answers a question posed in an earlier paper.
item.dc:creator: Leandro Candido

item.title: Quasinormal and hyponormal operators in the $\beta(H)$-class
item.description: arXiv:2610.13490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following \cite{BR} we study hyponormal operators in the strictly larger class $\beta(H)$ of operators whose restriction to every non-zero reducing subspace is norm attaining. The Weyl-type characterization of positive operators via the essential spectrum used in the absolutely norm attaining case is replaced by a well-ordering condition on the eigenvalues (Theorem~\ref{thm:positive}). We prove a transfinite, block-diagonal representation $T=\bigoplus_i\lambda_iS_i$ (with isometries $S_i$) for the $\beta(H)$-operators whose $|T|$-eigenspaces are reducing, equivalently the quasinormal operators with $|T|\in\beta(H)$, and we show by examples that hyponormality alone does not give such a decomposition. For normal operators we obtain a complete representation, and for hyponormal $\beta(H)$-operators we show that normality is equivalent to the spectrum having planar Lebesgue measure zero. An analogous area-zero criterion for normality is proved for hyponormal operators attaining the minimum modulus on every non-zero reducing subspace.
item.dc:creator: Ramesh Golla, Hiroyuki Osaka, Shanola S. Sequeira

item.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,\lambda \in (0,1)$: \[ \gamma_{\Sigma_1}(K)^{1-p} \gamma_{\Sigma_2}(L)^p \le \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-\lambda} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}{\lambda} \right)^p \right)^{n} \gamma_{\Gamma}((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L) , \] whenever $\Gamma \leq \Sigma_1 \sharp_p \Sigma_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \Gamma$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=\lambda$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: \[ \gamma(a K)^{1-\lambda} \gamma(b L)^{\lambda} \leq \gamma \left ( a^{1-\lambda} b^\lambda \left ((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Milman, Shohei Nakamura, Hiroshi Tsuji

item.title: The tensor product of the Fremlin tensor product of Banach lattice algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.13734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Arens regularity of the Fremlin projective tensor product of Banach lattice algebras. We firrst introduce and investigate L-weakly almost periodic functionals, a class of functionals defind in terms of L-weak compactness of their orbits. We obtain a characterization of these functionals in terms of bounded disjoint sequences and use it to analyze the Fremlin projective tensor product. In particular, we prove that, for nontrivial Banach attice algebras A and B, Arens regularity of A j jB implies Arens regularity of both A and B. The converse, however, fails: we construct two Arens regular Banach lattice algebras whose Fremlin projective tensor product is not Arens regular. We also establish several sufficient conditions for the Arens regularity of A j jB, including conditions involving the positive Schur property and order continuity of the norm on the space of regular operators. Finally, we show that when both factors are Banach f-algebras, their Fremlin projective tensor product is Arens regular.
item.dc:creator: Jamel Jaber, Marwa Troudi

item.title: Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman spaces in rearrangement-invariant and Hardy spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1981, Bourgain, Rosenthal, and Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of $L_p$ for $1 < p < \infty$, $p \neq 2$. We extend their construction to rearrangement-invariant spaces and Hardy spaces. For any separable rearrangement-invariant space $X$ with non-trivial Boyd indices, we show that these subspaces are complemented, previously obtained by Ghawadrah via a different argument, and establish the following dichotomy: Either one can extract an uncountable family of pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces, or they are all isomorphic to $X$. To this end, we introduce an ordinal index that detects whether $X$ embeds complementably into an arbitrary separable Banach space. On the other hand, we give sufficient conditions which imply that in certain spaces close to $L_1$ and $H^1$, these subspaces fail to be complemented.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Konstantos, Pavlos Motakis, Thomas Speckhofer

item.title: Best proximity point results of operator type condensing mappings via measure of noncompactness and application to an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncompactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.
item.dc:creator: Parveen Kumar, Ankit Kumar

item.title: A proof of Borcea's quadratic variance conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.12499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial of degree $n\ge2$, and let $\sigma_2(p)$ be the root mean square distance of its zeros from their centroid, including multiplicities. We prove that every zero of $p$ lies within distance $\sigma_2(p)$ of a critical point. This proves Borcea's quadratic conjecture and, in particular, gives a new proof of Sendov's conjecture. Two polynomial integration identities prove the result analytically for $n\ge2048$. For the remaining degrees, we derive explicit necessary inequalities, including a variable integration endpoint and an exact centered coefficient identity. Directed integer arithmetic certifies a finite covering of the resulting parameter domains. Degrees $4$--$26$ use $150\,845$ certified three-dimensional regions; degrees $27$--$2047$ use a further $27\,429$ regions, with degree intervals allowed. The cases of degree 2 and 3 were already covered by Khavinson--Pereira--Putinar--Saff--Shimorin.
item.dc:creator: Ludovick Bouthat, Shaun Fallat

item.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Khatana, Aditya Gahlawat, Naira Hovakimyan, Petros Voulgaris

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A bipartite observable is stable when its idealized responses are continuous. We show that it is NIP exactly when they are of the first Baire class. They then form a Rosenthal compactum, and the dividing lines of Shelah in model theory, together with the classification of Rosenthal compacta of Todor\v{c}evi\'c, acquire a physical meaning. For observables, mixtures of states make every hereditarily separable compactum of idealized responses metrizable, and the Todor\v{c}evi\'c trichotomy becomes a classification into three classes. Each class contains a physical order: the comparison of photon numbers, the comparison of positions, and the causal order of spacetime, whose idealized responses are not first countable because a light cone can shrink to a point; the comparison of two phases on a circle joins it there. Each of the seven minimal families of the heptachotomy, which Argyros, Dodos and Kanellopoulos extracted from the methods of Todor\v{c}evi\'c, is realized by a tree of preparations of photons, of a particle in a box, or of a spin chain read by a probe; the spin chain also shows that NIP, unlike its uniform version, is not symmetric between the two parties. Finally, for the Ising model in a transverse field we show that, in the ordered phase, the responses of the two pure phases form split pairs whose midpoints, the responses of the symmetric state, form an uncountable discrete set; the proof uses a Lee--Yang theorem for this model.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Sharp power-weight estimates for the fractional spherical maximal operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.13326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $0\leq\alpha<n$, let $A_{*}^{\alpha}$ denote the fractional spherical maximal operator. In this paper we characterise the range of $\beta$ for which the $L^p-L^q$ power-weight estimate \[\left\|A_{*}^{\alpha} f\right\|_{L^q(|x|^{q\beta})} \leq C \left\|f\right\|_{L^p(|x|^{p\beta})}\] holds. In the diagonal case $p=q$, our work gives an affirmative answer to a conjecture of Lee. We prove analogous results for the lacunary fractional spherical maximal operator.
item.dc:creator: Riju Basak, Surjeet Singh Choudhary, Chun-Yen Shen, Daniel Spector

item.title: Actions of Fell bundles, II: tensor products and Fourier-Stieltjes algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.13646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the context of Fell bundles over discrete groups, we introduce and analyze suitable notions of direct sum and tensor product of actions of Fell bundles on Hilbert bundles. For $C^*$-dynamical systems, where actions arise from equivariant representations, we discuss how the tensor product of two such actions is related to the action associated with the tensor product of the underlying equivariant representations. Likewise, since any action gives rise to a $C^*$-correspondence between the full cross-sectional $C^*$-algebras of the involved Fell bundles, we examine the connection between the $C^*$-correspondence associated with the tensor product of two given actions and the tensor product of the associated $C^*$-correspondences. We also discuss how the tensor product of actions naturally appears in Rieffel-like induction processes. Finally we present related results on the Fourier-Stieltjes and Fourier algebras of a Fell bundle.
item.dc:creator: Erik B\'edos, Roberto Conti

item.title: Restriction of Fractional Derivatives of the Fourier Transform
item.description: arXiv:2410.06092v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the differentiability of the Fourier transform of $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ at points on the graph of a function with non-vanishing Gaussian curvature. In particular, we show that if the values of $\widehat{f}$ along the graph possess $H^\ell$ Sobolev regularity, then this implies a certain degree of regularity of $\widehat{f}$ in the last coordinate direction as well. Two types of results are proved: One controls the $\beta$-order derivative in the last direction in terms of its $H^{-s}$ norm for suitable combinations of $(\beta, p, s, \ell)$. This extends the result in \cite{GoldStol}*{Theorem 1.12} to fractional derivatives and to some of its sharp endpoints. In particular, we recover the sharp range in the $s=0$ case where $\frac{\partial \widehat{f}}{\partial \xi_n}$ has a surface restriction in $L^2$. The second set of results is about $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ bounds for difference quotients and fractional difference quotients of $\widehat{f}$, generalizing results in \cite{G2016}.
item.dc:creator: Michael Goldberg, Chun Ho Lau

item.title: $J$-class weighted translations on locally compact groups
item.description: arXiv:2506.04730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A bounded linear operator $T$ on a Banach space $X$ (not necessarily separable) is said to be $J$-class operator whenever the extended limit set, say $J_T(x)$ equals $X$ for some vector $x\in X$. Practically, the extended limit sets localize the dynamical behavior of operators. In this paper, using the extended limit sets we will examine the necessary and sufficient conditions for the weighted translation $T_{a,\omega}$ to be $J$-class on a locally compact group $G$, within the setting of $ L^p$-spaces for $ 1 \leq p < \infty $. Precisely, we delineate the boundary between $J$-class and hypercyclic behavior for weighted translations. Then, we will show that for the torsion elements in locally compact groups, unlike the case of non-dense orbits of weighted translations, we have $J_{T_{a,\omega}}(0)=L^p(G)$. Finally, we will provide some examples on which the weighted translation $ T_{a,\omega}$ is $J$-class but it fails to be hypercyclic.
item.dc:creator: A. R. Imanzadeh Fard, M. R. Azimi, I. Akbarbaglu

item.title: Extension of Sobolev functions on balls in infinite dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2606.06229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Sobolev extension operator $E:W^{p,1}\left( B,P \right) \rightarrow W^{p,1}\left( \ell^{2} ,P \right)$ using a completely new method, where $B\subset \ell^{2}$ is the unit ball and $P$ is any non-trivial centered Gaussian measure on $\ell^{2}$. This solves an open problem posed in the literatures.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzhe Wang, Xu Zhang, Shiliang Zhao

item.title: On the Spectra of Multiplicative Hilbert Operator on Bergman Spaces of Dirichlet Series
item.description: arXiv:2608.22882v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $\alpha>1$, we study the weighted multiplicative Hilbert operator \[ (T_\alpha f)(s) = \int_{1/2}^{\infty} f(t)\bigl(\zeta(s+t)^\alpha-1\bigr) \left(t-\frac12\right)^{\alpha-1}\,dt \] on the Hilbertian Bergman space $A_{\alpha,0}^2$ of Dirichlet series with zero constant term. In the natural orthonormal basis, $T_\alpha$ is represented by the weighted multiplicative Hilbert matrix \[ \left( \frac{\Gamma(\alpha)\sqrt{d_\alpha(m)d_\alpha(n)}} {\sqrt{mn}\,(\log(mn))^\alpha} \right)_{m,n\ge2}, \] where $d_\alpha$ is the generalized divisor function defined by $\zeta(s)^\alpha=\sum_{n\ge1}d_\alpha(n)n^{-s}$ for $\Re s>1$. Set $\Lambda_\alpha=\Gamma(\alpha/2)^2/\Gamma(\alpha)$. We prove that the essential spectrum of \(T_\alpha\) is \([0,\Lambda_\alpha]\) and that the spectrum in this interval is purely absolutely continuous with multiplicity one. Above \(\Lambda_\alpha\), there are at most finitely many eigenvalues, all of which are simple. Moreover, there is a unique \(\alpha_*\in(1,2)\) such that \(T_\alpha\) has eigenvalues if and only if \(\alpha>\alpha_*\). Consequently, the associated sharp embedding inequality admits a non-zero extremizer precisely when $\alpha>\alpha_*$, and this extremizer is unique up to scalar multiplication. We also establish the asymptotic formula $\|T_\alpha\|\sim\Gamma(\alpha+1)/(2(2\log 2)^\alpha)$ as $\alpha\to\infty$. A key step in the proof combines Mellin-transform asymptotics, strict total positivity, and eigenvalue counting to exclude embedded eigenvalues. The proof includes a general result on the essential and singular continuous spectra of weighted integral Hankel operators.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Ma, Yufeng Lu, Chao Zu

item.title: On the equivalence of Sobolev norms in infinite dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2608.24702v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove dimension-free higher-order Sobolev norm estimates on open convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with respect to Gaussian measure and use them to obtain norm equivalence on nonempty open convex subsets of $\ell^2$ endowed with a nondegenerate Gaussian measure. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first such equivalence theorem on a proper open subset of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, beyond the earlier whole-space results. We also prove the Malliavin--Sobolev norm equivalence for all $p\in[1,\infty)$ and $k\ge2$, including the case $p=1$, $k\ge3$ left open by Addona--Muratori--Rossi in \cite{AddonaMuratoriRossi}.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzhe Wang

item.title: Morita Induction and Preservation of Geometric and Dynamical Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2608.30380v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given Banach algebras with bounded approximate identities that are Morita equivalent in the sense of Paravicini, we give explicit formulas for the induced correspondence of closed ideals, characterize it via localized Morita submodules, determine when corresponding ideals are Morita equivalent via restricted bimodules, and show that corresponding quotients are always Morita equivalent. We prove preservation of geometric cores associated to compatible dense algebraic cores. For equivalent \'etale groupoids with paracompact unit spaces, Morita induction preserves dynamical ideals and inner supports. For the Morita equivalence between the $\ell^p$ uniform Roe algebra and the $\ell^p$ uniform algebra, we prove that the latter has a bounded approximate identity of projections, identify its geometric ideals explicitly, and identify corresponding complete-lattice block decompositions of the full ideal lattices with matching extremal ideals. Under property A, or for $p=1$, these blocks collapse; for $p=2$, collapse of the minimal block characterizes property A.
item.dc:creator: Yeong Chyuan Chung, Xinhui Du

item.title: The Strong Naor--Schechtman Convolution Inequality on the Product of Cyclic Groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.15768v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we resolve the convolution inequality problem posed by Naor and Schechtman in \cite[Question 6.1]{N-S2016} (see also \cite{Na2016}). More precisely, we establish the following strong convolution inequality on products of finite cyclic groups: For each $1\leq p<\infty$ there exists $c_{p}>0$ such that for every $n$, $m\in \mathbb{N}$ the following holds \[ \begin{split} &\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x+\varepsilon)-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x-\varepsilon)\right|^{p}\\ \leq& c^{p}_{p}\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|\varepsilon_{j}\left[E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x+e_{j})-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x-e_{j})\right]\right|^{p}, \end{split} \] $E_{A}f(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{\delta\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}f\left(x+\sum_{j\in A}\delta_{j}e_{j}\right)$ for every $A\subseteq \{1,\cdots,n\}$. The growth order we obtain here $c_{p}=O(p)$ as $p\to \infty$. For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.
item.dc:creator: Yong Jiao, Sijie Luo, Dmitriy Zanin, Dejian Zhou

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
item.description: arXiv:2610.11002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When two quantum systems are prepared independently and each is driven to an idealized limit, the expectation of a bipartite observable may depend on which system is idealized first. We call an observable stable when it does not. We show that an observable is stable if and only if every idealized preparation of one system can be simulated to arbitrary accuracy, uniformly over all probes, by finite mixtures of actual preparations, provided that the probing system is idealized first; on stable observables, two idealized preparations have a unique, symmetric independent product. Under a uniform form of stability, the number of preparations that $n$ adaptive probes can tell apart at a fixed margin is bounded by a polynomial in $n$, and responses can be learned with a bounded number of mistakes; otherwise, at some margin, $n$ probes tell apart $2^n$ preparations. The swap test, Hong--Ou--Mandel coincidences and discrete equality tests are uniformly stable, with bounds independent of the dimension, while order comparisons of discrete spectra unbounded above are unstable. The proofs rest on the classical fact that a single double limit condition appears, under different names, in topology (Grothendieck), functional analysis (Krivine--Maurey), algebra (Arens), probability (Simons) and combinatorics (Pt\'ak), and in model theory as Shelah's stability; the independent product corresponds to Harrington's lemma. Model theory supplies a common language for these conditions; we use it as a Rosetta stone, pairing each physical question with its mathematical formulation.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights: weighted maximal inequalities and fundamental structural properties
item.description: arXiv:2509.23839v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal H_{\infty}^\delta$ denote the Hausdorff content of dimension $\delta\in(0,n]$ defined on subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. The principal problem, considered in this paper, is to characterize the non-negative function $w$ for which the weighted $L^p$ inequality with $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the weighted weak $L^1$ inequality on Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators associated with Hausdorff content hold true. To achieve this, we introduce a class of Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights, denoted as $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and then show that, for any $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\delta\in(0,n]$, the weighted $L^p$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and the weighted weak $L^1$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{1,\delta}$ by proposing a novel approach. As the second objective, applying this approach, the seminal structural properties of classical Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, such as the reverse H\"older inequality [R. R. Coifman and C. Fefferman, Studia Math. 51 (1974), 241-250], the self-improving property [B. Muckenhoupt, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 165 (1972), 207-226], and Jones' factorization theorem [P. W. Jones, Ann. of Math. (2) 111 (1980), 511-530], are all established for $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$. The main novelties of this paper lies in: (i) we discover $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$ weights with rich structural properties, that increase strictly on dimension exponent and hence reduce to the classical $A_p$ class at the endpoint dimension, forming proper subsets of it for smaller dimension exponent; (ii) by proposing a novel approach, this work naturally extends the classical theory beyond measure-theoretic frameworks, while also provides novel insights even when reduced to the classical $A_p$ weight case.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: Elementary commutator method for the Dirac equation with long-range perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2511.08209v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present direct and elementary commutator techniques for the Dirac equation with long-range electric and mass perturbations. The main results are absence of generalized eigenfunctions and locally uniform resolvent estimates, both in terms of the optimal Besov-type spaces. With an additional massless assumption, we also obtain an algebraic radiation condition of projection type. For their proofs, following the scheme of Ito-Skibsted, we adopt, along with various weight functions, the generator of radial translations as conjugate operator, and avoid any of advanced functional analysis, pseudodifferential calculus, or even reduction to the Schr\"odinger equation. The results of the paper would serve as a foundation for the stationary scattering theory of the Dirac operator.
item.dc:creator: Shinichi Arita, Kenichi Ito

item.title: Why does entropy drive evolution equations?
item.description: arXiv:2603.07653v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: `Entropy' appears as driving force in many different evolution equations, both deterministic and stochastic, and in these equations this `entropy' also takes different forms. We show how all these examples can be understood as different instances of a common principle: Entropy drives evolutions because it characterizes the invariant measure of an underlying stochastic process. This interpretation explains the appearance of entropy, the different forms that entropy takes in these equations, and how entropy `drives' these evolution equations. We illustrate this common structure with examples from stochastic processes, gradient flows, and GENERIC systems.
item.dc:creator: Mark A. Peletier

item.title: Just Previsions
item.description: arXiv:2605.10173v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Previsions are positively homogeneous functionals, and are generalized forms of integration functionals. We investigate previsions -- just previsions, not sublinear or superlinear previsions as in previous work. We show that every prevision can be expressed as an infimum of sublinear previsions, and as a supremum of superlinear previsions under mild conditions. This extends to homeomorphisms between spaces of previsions and certain hyperspaces over spaces of sublinear or superlinear previsions, which can also be characterized in terms of orthogonality relations, making the construction a variant of a double powerspace construction.
item.dc:creator: Jean Goubault-Larrecq

item.title: Sharp weighted norm estimates for the positive Bergman operator: the two-parameter case
item.description: arXiv:2608.01159v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We allow the exponent $\alpha$ that defines the positive Bergman operator on the upper half-plane to differ from the exponent $\gamma$ that defines the underlying weighted Lebesgue spaces. In this setting, we prove a sharp weak-type off-diagonal weighted inequality, with explicit and best-possible dependence on the B\'ekoll\'e--Bonami characteristic of the weight. We then deduce strong-type off-diagonal inequalities for the same operator. The key new tool is an off-diagonal extrapolation theorem, adapted to allow a change in the power of the distance to the boundary along the way.
item.dc:creator: Benoit F. Sehba

item.title: Limits of mapping packages and tangents of Sobolev maps
item.description: arXiv:2608.13124v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show the existence of ultralimits of sequences of Hajlasz-Sobolev mappings $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ when $X_i$ converges to a limit space in the pointed measured Gromov (pmG) sense, partially extending recent results in [T. Ikonen and S. Wenger, (2026), arXiv:2603.05246]. We moreover demonstrate that the mappings pmG-converge to the ultralimit in a suitable sense, and obtain Arzela-Ascoli theorems in the context of pmG-convergence. As an application, we establish a version of Preiss's phenomenon for Hajlasz-Sobolev maps $f:(X,\mu)\to V$ into arbitrary Banach spaces. Besides extending it to maps into infinite dimensional targets, our result generalizes existing versions of Preiss's phenomenon [G. C. David, Geom. Funct. Anal., 25 (2015)], [N. Gigli, A. Mondino, and T. Rajala, J. Reine Angew. Math., 705 (2015)] by establishing it for pointed measured Gromov-Hausdorff tangents without a doubling assumption.
item.dc:creator: Milica Cakovi\'{c}, Elefterios Soultanis
